## Diagnosis

- **coverage** (minor): PASS. All seven acceptance criteria land on a task that would actually produce or verify them, and no constitution clause is uncited. AC1 (fixture, prompt, pass condition per scenario) -> C-2 on T-004. AC2 (with and without the skill, delta graded) -> C-4 and C-12 on T-004, with C-10's second staged copy on T-001. AC3 (contradiction round trip) -> C-5, split T-002/T-004. AC4 (unacknowledged tension its own scenario) -> C-6, split T-002/T-004. AC5 (scope proposal across three tiers) -> C-7, split T-002/T-004. AC6 (nothing written to a real scope) -> C-10, split T-001/T-004, plus C-11's byte-identity snapshot on all four. AC7 (doc beside the other maintainer evals) -> C-1 and C-12 on T-004. The spec body's fourth behavior, 'whether generated summaries and entities are any good', maps to C-8 split T-003/T-004. Clause citation is complete in the other direction too: C-1 and C-11 on all four tasks, C-2/C-4/C-9/C-12 on T-004 alone (all doc-only clauses, correctly), C-13 on T-001 and T-004, which is exactly the scope C-13's own text names ('EVALS.md and the comments in eval-scope.sh'). Nothing in the spec is uncovered. The blocking defects below are all in how the cited clauses are checked, not in what is cited.

- **T-004** (blocker): FAIL. The check_method contradicts itself, and on the reading its second paragraph forces, the document-to-fixture binding for C-5, C-6, C-7 and C-8 is checked by nobody. Paragraph one says 'Every other cited clause is verified by its own check method as written in .agent-guild/state/constitution.md - read each clause's check field and run it. Do not paraphrase them here.' Paragraph two then paraphrases and narrows four of them: 'C-5, C-6, C-7, and C-8 are checked here against the document, having been checked against the fixtures upstream.' The fixture-facing conjunct of each of those four checks is precisely the conjunct that ties the document to the fixture, and upstream there was no document to tie it to. C-5's second conjunct is 'read the fixture to confirm it holds an accepted record that the planted input genuinely contradicts' - at T-002 that was checked against a fixture, with no scenario naming it. C-6's is 'read each row's fixture ... and confirm it makes that row's expected outcome the correct one' - there were no rows at T-002. C-7's is 'read each input against references/scope-decisions.md ... and confirm the reference routes it to the tier the scenario expects' - there was no scenario at T-002, and T-002's own half substitutes 'the tier the fixture was built to elicit'. C-8's is 'Identify the note the scenario grades and confirm the run emitted that note's extract' - T-003 could not identify it. So C-6's own failing example passes both halves: a doc that swaps the positive and negative rows between the two slugs satisfies T-004's half (the scenario exists and carries both rows) and satisfies T-002's half (the fixture is correctly built), and grades correct skill behavior as a failure. Same shape for C-5 (scenario names the Tier 2 fixture), C-7 (expected tokens paired with the wrong inputs), and C-8 (rows graded against a note whose extract was never emitted).

- **deps** (blocker): FAIL on concurrency, PASS on structure. The graph is a DAG - T-001, T-002 and T-003 have empty deps, T-004 depends on all three, no cycles, every referenced task exists, and T-004's dependency on all three is right (it must open every fixture and call the script). But the three leaf tasks are not independent at check time, and the task files assert otherwise. C-1's check reads the whole working tree diff, and C-11 runs three whole-repo smoke suites; three workers writing concurrently into the same tree means each task's checker sees the other two tasks' work. T-001 states this as a pass condition it will then fail: 'note this task delivers only eval-scope.sh, so a diff touching nothing else is the pass'. Once T-002 has landed a fixture directory, a diff touching something else is exactly what T-001's checker sees, and T-001 gets failed for T-002's work. T-002's and T-003's notes ('this task delivers only fixture directories under the evals path', 'one fixture directory') have the same shape and the same exposure to each other. C-11 is worse, because it is whole-repo and unqualified: an in-progress or lint-dirty fixture from a concurrent task turns another task's C-11 red, and the smoke suite's shasum snapshot at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:586 compares the fixtures tree to itself across a run, which a concurrent writer can perturb. Either serialize T-001 -> T-002 -> T-003 through deps, or restate the C-1 and C-11 notes on all three so they judge only this task's own artifacts and treat sibling paths as expected.

Whole-tree diff at .agent-guild/scripts/check-diff-scope.py:91-96. Shasum snapshot at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:586, compared at :1229.
- **T-002** (blocker): FAIL on sizing, and the excerpt's own packing advice hides an interference bug. One dispatch is asked for: a contradiction against an accepted record that amending makes sense for; both branches of the tension rule, each needing a slug across three or more prior notes; four scope-signal inputs routed to project, client, journal and a narrower-wins tiebreak; and, if the cross-project recurrence signal is used, a client root carrying two project directories whose notes actually name the subject. That is roughly six or more prior notes, several memory records, several inbox transcripts, and a two-level directory tree, all in realistic consulting prose, all matching the nanoid conventions, against four separate judgment clauses. A FAIL on any one clause reworks the whole thing, and the diagnosis will mix three unrelated behaviors. The excerpt makes it worse by suggesting the behaviors share a scope - 'One scope can serve several of the behaviors below, and a client root holding two project directories is a natural home for most of this' - without naming the interference that creates. C-6's positive case requires that no transcript in the groomed inbox names the slug out loud; SKILL.md:122 reads the transcript, not one designated file, so a contradiction transcript or a scope-signal transcript that happens to mention the open question silently kills the positive case. And one process-mode run over a shared inbox emits contradiction flags, tension flags and four candidate flags at once, entangling every scenario's delta and every scenario's C-4 baseline. Cut along clause lines, one fixture directory per task, with the directory name written into the task file so concurrent workers cannot collide and T-004 knows what to open: T-002a, the C-5 contradiction fixture; T-002b, the C-6 tension fixture (one scope, two slugs, one inbox that names the second aloud and not the first); T-002c, the C-7 scope-signal fixture, which is the one that needs the client root with two project directories.
